chapter: Early drum sets and dance-hall era
title: Records and phonographs growing up
summary: His family could not afford a phonograph; he heard records only at other people's houses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Did you listen to many records when you were a kid?

Well no, because we never had no autophonic, I know, used to call them graphimoles at the time. We didn't have any. All we had was that melodic in around the house, and he has to play that. At that time, I'd listen to, if I would hear a record, it'd be at somebody else's house or somebody else. You know, I'd listen to them. Just couldn't afford it, the old man had so many children, you know. It was 13, I was...
